title: RunAsPPL explicitly zeroed or removed
description: Detects RunAsPPL set to a decimal or hexadecimal zero, or deleted at its machine registry configuration location.

hypothesis.summary: An adversary may weaken LSASS protection by zeroing or removing RunAsPPL before attempting credential access; registry state alone does not establish effective protection.
hypothesis.rationale: Effective LSASS protection depends on operating-system defaults, policy, reboot state and UEFI lock; deleting a value does not prove protection was disabled.
hypothesis.detection_goal: Detects RunAsPPL set to a decimal or hexadecimal zero, or deleted at its machine registry configuration location.

data_sources.name: Microsoft Defender for Endpoint registry events

triage.summary: Effective LSASS protection depends on operating-system defaults, policy, reboot state and UEFI lock; deleting a value does not prove protection was disabled.
steps: Review the exact value, previous state where available, actor, initiating process and associated management-policy changes.
Verify effective protection on the device, including policy precedence, tamper protection, UEFI lock and reboot requirements.
Confirm the change owner and correlate with credential-access activity before escalation or an approved restoration.
false_positives: Approved security-policy rollback, compatibility troubleshooting or repeated application of an already-disabled configuration.

validation.expected_outcome: Match the bounded event, key/action/path or successful operation combination; reject one-field mutations, lookalikes and absent required fields. Synthetic tests do not establish live telemetry or production performance.

limitations: Effective LSASS protection depends on operating-system defaults, policy, reboot state and UEFI lock; deleting a value does not prove protection was disabled.
Current-revision evidence is synthetic only. Validate full generated KQL, source fields, ingestion delay, alert volume and scoped exclusions in the target before enabling.
